name: oddbout
description: Make, review and register your ODDBOUT fighter with a creation skill and runtime. Desktop MCP clients use the included connection; ChatGPT and Dots use the connected ODDBOUT App.

interface.longDescription: Connect your ODDBOUT account with Google and make a fighter in one place. Ask ODDBOUT to make one from your words or pictures (hosted generation: two looks, then the eleven motions, then registration), have it made on your own PC as a generation host, or create it yourself in your PC or a supported per-user Dots workspace with Node.js 22.12+, Python 3.11+ and your own generation account. Review looks and animation groups, resume unfinished work, register the approved package and manage your fighters with the same connected account. A chat without execution or file delivery cannot package animations itself; hosted generation does that for you.
defaultPrompt: Make an ODDBOUT fighter for me from this idea.
Resume my fighter and show what still needs review.

publication.release_notes: 0.6.10: fitSheets now fits total and per-asset byte/pixel budgets with actual measured trials after normalization; outputScale caps density. Preserve frames, timing, chosen encoding, original files and game size. Required validators and server limits are unchanged. 0.6.9: MCP packaging preparation and workspace inspection/build tools recover oversized sheets without regeneration. Bounded per-motion texture scaling preserves every frame, playback timing and apparent game size; requires the deployed texture-resolution-1 contract. Original assets remain unchanged. 0.6.8: Lossless WebP-only intermediate packs avoid duplicate PNG storage; explicit intermediate budgets up to 200 MB keep final upload limits unchanged. Packaging and creation progress require file/contract checks only. Missing, failed or stale gait/visual diagnostics no longer block; reports and user selections are preserved. Existing required/engine-loop plans work without a visual override or regeneration. 0.6.7: Explicit per-command public game-context file handoff verifies source, hashes and freshness while retaining revision and motion-quality gates. Distinguish Grok device login from host execution permission; preserve existing runtimes and results. Context CLIs use direct-fd JSON output on restricted Node pipes. 0.6.6: Dots gait review accepts the contract's variable cycles (walk 12-32, run 10-16 frames) instead of requiring 16/12, so a valid cycle is not resampled to fit; every actual frame still needs its own phase; contact and visual review remain required, and review evidence stays bound to the final pixels and timing. The kit guide names the current version. 0.6.5: Game-context fetches use the host HTTP(S) proxy, NO_PROXY and CA settings. Host execution permission remains separate; preserve active Dots runtimes, sessions, jobs and results. The ZIP also includes the Codex Git plugin installation guide. 0.6.4: Reuse the existing cloud App and its creation skill; the source ZIP is optional workspace/desktop tooling, not a second ChatGPT/Dots plugin. Clarify connection-only checks and verified cleanup of the old private ZIP plugin. 0.6.3: Clarify that the ZIP MCP connection is for desktop clients; ChatGPT and Dots need the connected ODDBOUT App, with the creation skill added to that App. 0.6.2: Separate server discovery, ZIP publication, host plugin installation, conversation tool exposure and native account verification. Preserve existing connections; diagnose missing tools without local-login or generation fallback. 0.6.1: Updated unified cloud MCP and local CLI guidance, including migration. Existing-fighter package updates retain identity and history; the creator homepage requires separate normal website sign-in. 0.6.0: The source plugin includes hosted ODDBOUT MCP configuration (https://mcp.oddbout.com/mcp, Google sign-in) for desktop MCP clients, alongside the creation skill; ChatGPT and Dots require an App connection. Verify the installed replacement and its native get_profile in the intended conversation before any explicitly requested removal of an older connection. 0.5.5: Pinned Dots VM entry and resume, Grok subscription route, private original delivery, plugin-cache launcher repair. VM creation acceptance remains separate from installation and unit checks. 0.5.4: A running generation can be stopped and has a time limit, so a stuck provider no longer blocks the motion; readiness checks run together and check for kit updates at most every five minutes; unchanged files are not hashed again. 0.5.3: Packing and gait checks run faster; an approved device sign-in survives a network failure and finishes with --device-wait; recording a version after an interrupted copy works; saving the session retries a briefly locked file on Windows; updates that change the validator or tools ask for a restart. 0.5.2: A session lock left by an interrupted run is reclaimed instead of blocking the session; parallel tool calls wait their turn; a finished generation is always recorded; game-context failures say whether the kit needs an update; profile text limits match the package contract. 0.5.1: fighter:pack and fighter:gait run again (0.5.0 left out a module they import), and a package that fails file validation is no longer written to its folder. 0.5.0: The sprite-gen engine is now sprite-gen-agent (Alex Kim's sprite-gen 3.4.0 with the motion engine); no hash patch step. 0.4.0: One ODDBOUT entry point for creation, grouped review and registration. Run the same workspace tools from a PC or a supported Dots workspace without a separate local MCP plugin. Use the existing connected ODDBOUT account for registration; preserve local projects and selected versions.
